Thanks again for taking the time today — good session. Quick recap from our discovery and initial recommendations so we can align on prioritization before the technical deep-dive: 

Key takeaways from call:
- You want a customer-facing assistant that reliably cites internal docs and returns grounded answers (SLA: 200ms P95 inference for short responses; tolerate higher P95 for long-form).
- Primary content sources: internal product docs, release notes, and policies (PDF + Confluence).
- Concern: hallucination on policy/legal content is a blocker; grounding/citation coverage is the top quality metric.

Initial model & infra recommendations:
- Embedding model: rw-embed-4-small (balanced accuracy + cost).
- Generation models (recommend starting A/B):
  - redwood-2-medium (lower cost, good latency)
  - redwood-2-large (higher quality, more compute)
- Reranker: cross-encoder-rw-small-v2 (good precision@1 vs latency tradeoff).
- Retrieval settings (starter config): chunk_size=500 tokens, overlap=50 tokens, top_k_retrieval=12, reranker_top_k=5.

Evaluation & metrics to track (we'll provide a benchmark dashboard):
- Grounding rate: % answers with at least one correct citation (target >= 95% for desktop help queries).
- Precision@1 and NDCG for reranker/retreival combo.
- Hallucination / factual error rate on policy questions (target < 2%).
- Latency: token-level cost and P95 tail.

Included: I've attached the prompt set we discussed (acme_rag_prompt_set_v1.json) and our internal benchmark snapshot (redwood_benchmark_20270401.pdf). Also linking the dashboard: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-rag-2027

2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Vivek and Neha to validate retrieval pipeline and discuss reranker latency trade-offs (I added tentative times in the calendar invite).
3) We will run a small A/B bench (redwood-2-medium vs redwood-2-large) on your prompt set and return results within 7 business days.

Hi Bob — copying in technical details to address your questions. Short answers up front: cross-encoder-rw-small-v2 is a reasonable starting point for precision and has ~40–80ms per document-pair on modern GPUs (batch optimized). End-to-end P95 will depend on retrieval top_k and reranker_top_k; with top_k_retrieval=12 and reranker_top_k=5 we typically see end-to-end P95 in the ~180–320ms range depending on model size and batching. We can hit your 200ms target with the redwood-2-medium generation model + optimized batching and a small cross-encoder reranker, or by moving reranking to async with cached reranks for common queries.

Detailed notes: 
- Embeddings: precompute embeddings for static docs (recommended). For frequently changing docs, do nearline updates. Precomputing avoids extra latency and reduces cost at query time.
- Chunking: for long PDFs, chunk ~500 tokens with 50-token overlap is conservative; for policy/legal we sometimes use 800-token chunks with 100-token overlap to preserve paragraph coherence but that increases retrieval noise. If citations must precisely map to sections, use smaller chunks and include a mapping table to original doc offsets.
- Reranker choice: 
  - cross-encoder-rw-small-v2: best precision@1 / moderate latency. Good default.
  - bi-encoder + lightweight cross-encoder cascade: fast at recall stage, then cross-encoder for top candidates; useful if you need lower latency and have heavy QPS.
- Grounding metrics we recommend capturing in the first week of tests:
  - Grounding rate (citations per answer)
  - Correct-citation precision (are the citations actually relevant)
  - Hallucination flagging: run a small human eval set against known gold answers (we can help run this)
  - Regression checks: store prompt-level metrics and enable daily alerting if grounding rate drops > 3% vs baseline.

Benchmark plan: we'll spin up a focused A/B run for your priority prompt set. Deliverables: 
- Bench dashboard (link) comparing redwood-2-medium vs redwood-2-large across grounding rate, precision@1, latency P50/P95, token costs.
- Reranker matrix (attached) showing precision/latency tradeoffs for candidate rerankers.

I'll coordinate with Neha to get the attachment/ingestion checklist and a short runbook for precomputing embeddings.

—Vivek
